benchmarks.verdict: The five 500Hz QD-OLEDs TechSpot compared perform similarly (>300 nits SDR, HDR panel dimming); MAG 272QP X50 is the value pick, G60SF for matte; no 360Hz 1440p model recommended.

notes: 500Hz QD-OLEDs (GIGABYTE FO27Q5P, ASUS XG27AQDPG, MSI MPG 271QR X50 / MAG 272QP X50, Samsung G60SF) share the same Samsung Display panel: 300-nit SDR, True Black 500, ~108% DCI-P3 measured; differences are firmware/features. FO27Q5P is the best-equipped GIGABYTE (2x DP 2.1 + DP out, 2x HDMI 2.1, USB-C, KVM, 2x5W speakers, mic jack, 3y burn-in) – the only one in segment with speakers; MSI MPG X50 has stronger USB-C (98W) and DP 2.1. ASUS XG27AQDPG and FO27Q5P are the brightest SDR (~500 nits 25% window, Tom's). Input lag (Tom's, same method): LG 27GX790A 10 ms < XG27AQDPG 16 ms = G60SF 16 ms < FO27Q5P 18 ms < AW2725DF 19 ms. 360Hz models (FO27Q3, MO27Q3, AW2725DF) are previous Gen-3 QD-OLED, 250 nits/True Black 400 and now mostly price-competes vs ~$600-700 500Hz models. LG 27GX790A is WOLED MLA+ 480Hz: higher HDR highlights, less gamut (~96% P3), 2-yr warranty. Value: FO27Q5P street ~£600 (KitGuru) but $1,569 Amazon listing at Tom's review time (likely third-party) – US pricing needs checking. Gaps: RTINGS numeric data did not render via WebFetch; TFTCentral/PCMonitors are video reviews (no numbers); no reputable review found for GIGABYTE MO27Q3 (likely same panel as FO27Q3); MSI/ASUS warranty from spec sheets/TechSpot. Display Ninja and KitGuru used to fill gaps.
